anti-pattern — assuming Mapbox v2 features work in MapLibre,skills/maplibre-mapbox-migration/SKILL.md,"I was using Mapbox GL JS v2 in my app, including map.setFog() and some v2-specific camera features. After migrating to MapLibre, these are broken. Did I do something wrong in the migration?

You didn’t miss a step – the problem is that **MapLibre GL JS never shipped the Mapbox-v2-only APIs** like `map.setFog()` or the “free-camera” helpers. Those methods exist only in Mapbox GL JS v2 (and later v3) and were never added to the MapLibre fork.

To get the same visual effect you have to use the **MapLibre equivalents** (`setSky` for fog/atmosphere) and the **new camera-option helpers** (`calculateCameraOptionsFrom…` + `jumpTo/easeTo/flyTo`). The rest of your migration (package, namespace, token, style URL, etc.) is probably already correct.
Below is a **step-by-step guide** that shows exactly how to replace those two groups of APIs, plus a quick sanity-check checklist so you can be sure the rest of the migration is solid.

column4: MapLibre GL JS (v6-current)
**No `setFog`**. Atmosphere is expressed with the **`sky`** layer and the method `map.setSky({ … })`.

**No `FreeCameraOptions`**. Use the **camera-option calculators** (`calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation`, `calculateCameraOptionsFromTo`, etc.) and then call `jumpTo`, `easeTo`, or `flyTo`.
`sky` object (experimental) in the style JSON.
`maplibregl` (or direct imports)
Not required; you supply any keys that the tile source itself needs.

column1: Because MapLibre was forked from **Mapbox GL JS v1.13**, any API that first appeared in **v2** never existed in the MapLibre code base. The migration guide therefore tells you to replace those calls with the MapLibre equivalents rather than “just import the same method”.
Add a **`sky`** layer to your style (or edit the existing style JSON). A minimal sky definition looks like this:
* `sky-type` can be `""gradient""` or `""atmosphere""` – the latter gives you fog-like blending.
* All the fog-related properties from Mapbox (`color`, `horizon-blend`, etc.) map to the `sky-atmosphere-*` paint properties.
* The `sky` layer must be **the last layer** in the style (or at least after any raster layers you want the sky to appear behind).
You can edit the JSON by hand, or use **Maputnik** (the MapLibre style editor) to add a sky layer visually.
If you were doing something like:
// maplibregl is the namespace you imported
// The same visual intent, but using the sky-spec property names

`setSky` can be called any time after the map has loaded (e.g. inside `map.on('load', …)`). If you need to change the sky dynamically (e.g., day/night), just call `setSky` again with new values.
const cam = map.getFreeCameraOptions();   // {center, zoom, pitch, bearing, altitude, roll}

MapLibre’s camera model is still `center`, `zoom`, `pitch`, `bearing`, **plus** `elevation` (altitude) and `roll` (added in v5). There is **no mutable object** you can fetch and edit; instead you **calculate a new `CameraOptions` object** and feed it to a movement method.

map.getRoll ? map.getRoll() : 0   // roll (if you need it)
// 2️⃣ Apply it – you can use jumpTo (instant) or easeTo/flyTo (animated)
#### 3.2.2 “Look-at” from one point to another (the classic free-camera use-case)

> **Tip:** `calculateCameraOptionsFromTo` is available since v2.4.0 (MapLibre) and is the direct replacement for the Mapbox “free camera” look-at helper.
